summary:
Orbital Odyssey is an online 2.5D browser game with no installation to download, and it is single player mode. It's written in vanilla HTML5/CSS/JS with custom 2.5D isometric SVG graphics and synthesized Web Audio and makes aerospace systems engineering an interactive 4-minute game from concept to flight.

Directly addressing the challenge through JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and NASA's Four Mission Segments, players choose between a 1.0 AU Earth Explorer CubeSat mission (NASA CSLI CubeSat 101) and a 5.2 AU Europa Ocean Voyager flagship mission (Europa Clipper). Players combine payloads, solar/RTG power, radios, and launch vehicles, while real Tsiolkovsky rocket Δv and inverse-square sunlight physics (3.7% irradiance at Jupiter) pose challenges, they steer through launch staging, they survive three deep-space emergencies and they compare their build to real spacecraft that were built by NASA.

This project aims to make hands-on spacecraft engineering accessible to the students of Bahrain and the rest of the world without the need for expensive lab equipment or software.
details:
Orbital Odyssey is a 2.5D browser-based space mission design game structured around NASA JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and NASA's Four Mission Segments. Players choose between an Earth Explorer CubeSat mission (1.0 AU, modeled on NASA CSLI CubeSat 101) and a Europa Ocean Voyager flagship mission (5.2 AU, modeled on Europa Clipper), assembling payloads, power systems, radios, and launch vehicles in an interactive 2.5D workshop. Instead of relying on static quizzes, our creative approach turns authentic physics, specifically the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation for Δv mass ratios and the inverse-square law dropping solar irradiance to 3.7% at Jupiter, into live engineering trade-offs. After passing pre-flight validation, players steer their rocket through launch staging and multitask through three deep-space emergencies (planetary eclipses, cosmic-ray memory bit-flips, and Deep Space Network frequency locking) while capturing orbital anomaly photos, concluding with a mission debrief that matches their spacecraft to real NASA missions.

Built with zero external dependencies using vanilla HTML5, CSS3, ES6 JavaScript, a custom 2.5D isometric SVG renderer, and procedural Web Audio API sound synthesis (with demo video editing in DaVinci Resolve), the game runs instantly in any browser without expensive lab hardware. Our intended impact is to make hands-on aerospace systems engineering accessible to students across Bahrain (supporting STEM education aligned with the Bahrain Space Agency) and worldwide, balancing cognitive load with a toggleable Simple/Detailed Specs view and an interactive tutorial. In accordance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, generative AI tools (Claude, Manus AI, ChatGPT, and Gemini) were used to assist with code debugging, UI refinement, and Web Audio parameter tuning, while all mission concepts, mechanics, and media were directed by SpacePals II.
